Configuration.AuthFlowNote: Primary/documented connector auth is HTTP Basic Auth (securitySchemes.basicAuth, type=http/scheme=basic) where the 'username' is '{email_address}/token' and the 'password' is the agent's API token: Authorization: Basic base64({email_address}/token:{api_token}). This is Zendesk's standard API-token pattern (confirmed via the -u {email_address}/token:{api_token} curl example repeated 5x across the Ticketing OAS). A separate OAuth 2.0 bearer-token flow exists for public/marketplace apps (see OAuth2Alternate) but Basic w/ API token is the default, simplest, and most common integration path and does not expire.

OAuth2Alternate.note: POST https://{subdomain}.zendesk.com/oauth/tokens exchanges an authorization_code (from the browser redirect to /oauth/authorizations/new with response_type=code&client_id=&redirect_uri=&scope=), a refresh_token, or client_id+client_secret (client_credentials) for an access_token. access_token is then sent as 'Authorization: Bearer <access_token>'. Requires an OAuth Client registered in Zendesk Admin Center (client_id/client_secret). The password-grant flow is deprecated/discouraged. expires_in bounds: 300s-172800s (defaults null = server default); refresh_token_expires_in bounds: 604800s-7776000s (default 2592000s/30d).

Configuration.TokenRefreshStrategyNote: Only applicable when the OAuth2 authorization-code flow is used: POST /oauth/tokens with grant_type=refresh_token + refresh_token + client_id + client_secret rotates the access_token before expiry. The default Basic/API-token auth path (AuthFlow=basic) has no expiry and therefore no refresh step -- the API token is a long-lived credential managed by the Zendesk admin.
Configuration.APIBaseURLNote: Every Zendesk account is reached at a per-tenant subdomain of zendesk.com (OpenAPI 'servers' block: https://{subdomain}.{domain}.com, domain defaulting to 'zendesk'). The connector reads the tenant's subdomain from the per-connection Configuration key named 'Subdomain' (NOT baked into this vendor-wide metadata file) and substitutes it into the template to build every request URL. Gotcha: Zendesk also supports host-mapped custom domains for the AGENT-FACING web UI, but the API (and the OAuth authorize endpoint) must always be reached via the core '{subdomain}.zendesk.com' host, not the host-mapped domain -- confirmed explicitly in the OAuth authorization-page doc ('{subdomain} is your Zendesk core subdomain, not a host-mapped subdomain').

universalPK.note: Every top-level resource observed in the OAS (TicketObject, UserObject, OrganizationObject, GroupObject, and effectively all other resource schemas) declares its primary key as 'id: integer(int64), readOnly'. This is a consistent vendor-wide convention across both the Ticketing and Help Center APIs.

primary.requestParamShape: page[size]=<n>&page[after]=<cursor> (also page[before]=<cursor> for the previous page)
primary.note: Confirmed directly from the CursorPaginationPage request-parameter schema and the CursorPaginationMeta / Pagination response schemas in the Ticketing OAS. Many list endpoints (the 'DualPaginationPage' parameter) accept EITHER this cursor form OR the legacy integer '?page=N' form on the SAME 'page' query parameter name -- mutually exclusive per request. Newer endpoints (audits, incremental-adjacent list endpoints) are cursor-ONLY.

legacyOffsetFallback.note: Confirmed via the 'Page'/'PerPage' request-parameter schemas and the 'OffsetPaginationObject' response schema (count / next_page / previous_page, where next_page and previous_page are FULL URLs to follow directly, not just numbers). Only viable up to a vendor-documented depth on some endpoints (e.g. Search Requests errors with a 422 'Insufficient Resource Error' past page 11 at 100/page = 1000 total); the Rate Limits page also independently rate-limits 'List Tickets ?page={num}' pagination beyond page 500 to 50 requests/minute. Cursor pagination is the vendor-recommended default for new integrations; the offset form is a fallback for endpoints/older integrations that still expose it.

Configuration.APIVersioningNote: The API version is embedded directly in the URL path segment: /api/v2/... (confirmed via every path in both the Ticketing and Help Center OpenAPI specs). There is no header-based or accept-header-based versioning scheme; v2 has been the stable version for the entire observed spec.

cursorBased.seedParam: start_time (unix epoch seconds; must be at least 1 minute in the past; required ONLY on the first/seed request)
cursorBased.continuationParam: cursor (opaque; required on every subsequent request instead of start_time)
cursorBased.note: Confirmed directly from the OptionalIncrementalUnixTime/IncrementalCursor parameter schemas and the CursorBasedExportIncrementalTicketsResponse schema (after_cursor / after_url / before_cursor / before_url / end_of_stream / <resource-array>). Loop while end_of_stream=false, feeding the returned after_cursor as the next request's cursor param; stop (and persist the last after_cursor as the sync watermark) when end_of_stream=true.

timeBasedLegacy.responseEndTimePath: end_time (unix epoch of the last record in this page -- feed as the NEXT request's start_time)
timeBasedLegacy.note: Confirmed via the TimeBasedExportIncrementalTicketsResponse/TimeBasedExportIncrementalUsersResponse schemas (count / end_of_stream / end_time / next_page / <resource-array>). Zendesk's own guide explicitly recommends the cursor-based variant over this one for consistent performance and response sizes; use only where an object family has no cursor variant (ticket_events, ticket_metric_events, organizations as of this audit).

Configuration.WebhooksNote: Zendesk has a first-class Webhooks product/API (separate from the Ticketing 'Targets' resource captured in this connector's IO set) for outbound event notifications. Not modeled as a syncable IO in this connector (see OutOfScopeObjectFamilies -- 'Webhooks, Apps Framework, Integration Services, Amazon EventBridge': push-config/extension mechanisms, not data to sync), but recorded here because it is a real vendor capability a future push-based sync mode could use.
Configuration.WebhooksSignatureNote: Signature = base64(HMAC-SHA256(signing_secret, TIMESTAMP + BODY)). Verify by recomputing the same HMAC over the X-Zendesk-Webhook-Signature-Timestamp header value concatenated with the raw request body, then comparing (constant-time) to X-Zendesk-Webhook-Signature. GET/DELETE webhook requests may have an empty body.
Configuration.BulkOperationsNote: Zendesk's bulk-write convention is a per-resource verb SUFFIX, not a single shared batch base path (contrast HubSpot's one shared '/batch/*' path). Confirmed real, spec-declared endpoints across ~20 resources (tickets, users, organizations, organization_memberships, group_memberships, macros, triggers, automations, views, dynamic_content variants, suspended_tickets, deleted_tickets, workspaces, custom-object triggers, and more). '_many' endpoints queue an async background job polled via /api/v2/job_statuses/{id} (job_status resource) rather than returning inline results for the largest operations (e.g. Update Many, Create Many); some smaller ones (e.g. show_many, up to ~100 ids) return synchronously.

body.description: string -- human-readable detail (present on many, not all, classic-shape error bodies)

classic.note: Confirmed directly from multiple in-spec 400/409/422 response examples (e.g. Ticket Content Pins: 400={error:{message,title}} variant; 409={error:'ContentPinCreationConflict', description:'...'}; 422={error:'ContentAlreadyPinned', description:'...'}). The exact sub-shape of 'error' varies per endpoint -- sometimes a plain string code, sometimes a nested {message,title} object -- so parse defensively (string OR object).

body.errors: array of { id, status, code, title, detail, source, links } -- 'code' and 'title' are required per-item

jsonApiStyle.note: Confirmed from the 'Error'/'Errors' component schemas, used by newer resources (e.g. Approval Requests: ApprovalRequestErrors on 422).

rateLimitHeaders.note: On 429 Too Many Requests, Zendesk returns a Retry-After header (seconds to wait) plus account rate-limit headers (X-Rate-Limit / X-Rate-Limit-Remaining, duplicated as lowercase ratelimit-limit / ratelimit-remaining / ratelimit-reset on Ticketing APIs specifically). Some endpoints also expose an endpoint-scoped header, e.g. 'zendesk-ratelimit-tickets-index: total=100;remaining=99;resets=41'. Job-queue limits (the '_many' async endpoints) use a separate 'zendesk-ratelimit-inflight-jobs' header (max 30 concurrent queued/running jobs) and a distinct 'TooManyJobs' error body.

CustomObjectMarkerPattern.note: Unlike HubSpot's 'p_<portalId>_<name>' convention, Zendesk Custom Objects (/api/v2/custom_objects) are identified purely by a customer-chosen 'key' with no vendor-enforced prefix or namespace marker. Every record returned by the custom_objects list endpoint IS a customer-defined object by construction -- there is no built-in/custom split to detect within that endpoint.

ticketFields.note: TicketFieldObject.removable=false marks a system field present on all tickets; removable=true (the default/absence case) marks a customer-created custom ticket field. Confirmed directly from the TicketFieldObject schema description: 'If false, this field is a system field that must be present on all tickets.'

userAndOrganizationFields.note: UserFieldObject / OrganizationFieldObject carry no 'removable' (or equivalent) flag in the OAS. The /api/v2/user_fields and /api/v2/organization_fields endpoints only ever return customer-defined custom fields -- Zendesk's built-in user/organization attributes (name, email, role, etc.) are first-class properties on the User/Organization object itself, not entries in these field-definition lists. So every row from these two endpoints is a custom field by construction.

WriteCapability.create: Yes -- POST on the collection path for the large majority of writable resources (tickets, users, organizations, groups, macros, triggers, automations, views, custom objects/fields/records, targets, sla_policies, and more -- see per-IO SupportsCreate/CreateAPIPath).
WriteCapability.update: Yes -- PUT (not PATCH) on the single-record path for updatable resources (Zendesk uses PUT for partial updates throughout the observed spec).
WriteCapability.delete: Yes -- DELETE on the single-record path for most deletable resources; see DeleteSemantics for the soft-vs-hard split.
WriteCapability.batch: Yes -- see BulkOperationsAvailable/BulkOperationsBasePath ('_many' suffix convention, some synchronous, some async-job-based).

Configuration.ConcurrencyControlNote: No HTTP ETag / If-Match / If-Unmodified-Since header mechanism is exposed anywhere in the OAS. The one documented exception is Tickets: the update request body accepts an optional 'updated_stamp' (the ticket's last-known updated_at) plus 'safe_update' (boolean); when safe_update=true and updated_stamp does not match the ticket's current updated_at, Zendesk rejects the update as a collision. This is an application-level optimistic-concurrency field (closest to 'version' semantics), confirmed ONLY for Tickets -- no other of the 99 in-scope objects expose an equivalent field in this audit. Because the vendor-wide default is none, conflict handling should default to snapshot-3-way; the Tickets-specific updated_stamp/safe_update mechanism can be layered on as a Tickets-only enhancement.

DeleteSemanticsDetail.tickets: soft-then-purge -- DELETE /api/v2/tickets/{id} moves the ticket to the 'deleted_tickets' list (recoverable via POST /api/v2/deleted_tickets/restore_many); DELETE /api/v2/deleted_tickets/destroy_many performs the permanent purge ('If the job succeeds, the ticket is permanently deleted. This operation can't be undone.'). Deletion rate limit: 400 tickets/minute via the single-record DELETE.
DeleteSemanticsDetail.users: soft-then-purge -- deleted users appear in GET /api/v2/deleted_users ('Returns deleted users, including permanently deleted users'), with a documented permanent-purge rate of 700 users per 10 minutes. Mirrors the tickets pattern.
DeleteSemanticsDetail.suspendedTickets: soft (staging area, not a delete at all) -- suspended (undeliverable/spam-flagged) tickets can be recovered (POST /api/v2/suspended_tickets/recover_many) or permanently destroyed (destroy_many).
DeleteSemanticsDetail.otherResources: hard -- DELETE on organizations, groups, macros, triggers, automations, views, custom objects/records, targets, sla_policies, and the remaining majority of writable resources removes the record with no documented archive/recovery flag or staging list in the OAS.
DeleteSemanticsDetail.note: Cascading child deletes for parent-child resources happen asynchronously: 'child records are soft-deleted first and then permanently deleted after a 30-day retention period' (confirmed in-spec), though the parent-level DELETE call itself returns immediately.

Configuration.DefaultConflictResolutionReason: ConcurrencyControl=none for the vendor as a whole (no ETag/version on 98 of 99 objects), which rules out a reliable MostRecent resolution. DestWins is the safe default when/if bidirectional sync is later enabled: on pull, the MJ destination reflects Zendesk's own source-of-truth state. The one exception (Tickets' updated_stamp/safe_update) could support a Tickets-only MostRecent/collision-aware policy in a future enhancement, but is not broad enough to change the vendor-wide default.

RateLimitPolicy.helpCenterAPI: Same per-plan limits as the Support API, but tracked on a SEPARATE counter -- Help Center API calls do not consume the Support API's rate-limit budget and vice versa.

endpointOverrides.PUT /api/v2/tickets/{id}.json: 30 updates per 10 minutes per user per ticket
endpointOverrides.GET /api/v2/views/{view_id}/execute.json: 5 requests per minute, per view, per agent
endpointOverrides.GET /attachments/token/{token}: 2500 requests per minute (10/min per upload for uploads not associated with a ticket/comment)

RateLimitPolicy.appsRateLimit: API requests made by Zendesk Apps (not applicable to this connector, which is not a Zendesk App) are separately limited to 100 requests/minute/user/app at the client level and 700 calls/5 minutes/user/app at the API level.
RateLimitPolicy.accountWideCeiling: 100,000 requests per minute across ALL sources for the account (DoS-style anti-abuse ceiling, not a normal operating budget).
RateLimitPolicy.retryHeader: Retry-After (seconds) on every 429 response; the connector must honor it.
RateLimitPolicy.note: BatchMaxRequestCount=200 / BatchRequestWaitTime=60 (root fields) reflect the 'Team' plan tier -- the lowest CURRENT (non-legacy) Support-plan rate limit -- as a safe, provable default. A customer on a higher plan (Professional/Enterprise/High Volume) will under-utilize their real limit at this default; the connector should read the X-Rate-Limit / X-Rate-Limit-Remaining response headers at runtime and adapt upward rather than relying solely on this static default.

OutOfScopeObjectFamilies.Reason: Separate real-time chat product with its own API surface (/api-reference/live-chat/); not part of the Support/Guide ticketing+content data model in scope.
Separate voice/telephony product (/api-reference/voice/talk-api/); call records/IVR config, not ticketing data.
Entirely separate CRM product (/api-reference/sales-crm/) with its own leads/deals/contacts data model — explicitly excluded even from Zendesk's own public Postman workspace.
BI/analytics product layered on top of Support data — read-only reporting views, not a source-of-truth data model; no public write API.

Confirmed separate product with its own OpenAPI spec repo (github.com/zendesk/sunshine-conversations-api-spec) — real-time conversational messaging, structurally distinct from the ticketing/Guide model.
Conversational-AI product layer (/api-reference/ai-agents/); configuration/analytics for bot behavior, not core ticketing data.
Client-side embed configuration, not server-side syncable business data.

OutOfScopeObjectFamilies.Reason: Extension/notification mechanisms (push config), not data to sync.
Confirmed to duplicate the Ticketing OAS's own Custom Objects/Custom Object Fields/Custom Object Records tags (same objects, different landing page) — not a separate product, not double-counted.
